what: Copart runs online auctions for damaged and salvage vehicles. Insurers send it cars written off after accidents; it stores them on its yards and auctions them to dismantlers, rebuilders and buyers worldwide.
customers: Insurance companies and fleet owners selling vehicles, and dismantlers, rebuilders, dealers and exporters buying them.
money: auction, storage, towing and processing fees
vehicles it buys and resells on its own account
moat: Hundreds of large yards near major cities, bought as land rather than leased, where permits for new salvage yards are nearly impossible to obtain.
risks: Revenue was flat last year as used car values fell from their peak
Fewer accidents from safer cars would reduce long-term volumes
Insurance total-loss rates drive volume and can shift
opportunities: Operating margin of 35% and net margin of 32%, extraordinary for a physical business
Cars are more expensive to repair, so insurers write off a higher share of damaged vehicles
Cash of about $1.9 billion against almost no debt
watch: Unit volumes processed and average selling price per vehicle.
